scope: Bounded HAOS-IIP recoverability predictions. These are diagnostic records, not proofs of new physics or biology.

prediction_levels.P0_toy_internal: Supported only by toy or in-repo demonstrations.
prediction_levels.P1_cross_system: Supported across more than one toy or internal system.
prediction_levels.P2_external_dataset: Ready for external data or third-party benchmark tests.
prediction_levels.P3_field_facing: A field-facing diagnostic prediction with clear controls.
prediction_levels.P4_physics_candidate: A candidate physics-facing prediction requiring external replication.

records.title: Recoverability loss precedes visible failure under controlled perturbation
records.prediction_statement: In bounded interacting systems, a sustained recoverability collapse index should appear before visible or conventional failure under controlled monotone perturbation.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a field-facing diagnostic candidate: it predicts an ordering between recoverability loss and visible failure, not a new substrate or new physical law.
records.perturbation: A deterministic monotone perturbation sweep from intact baseline to maximum stress.
pass_criteria: k_star is defined before first visible_failure
result is deterministic across repeated runs
fail_criteria: recoverability is flat or non-informative under perturbation
the result changes across deterministic reruns
falsifiers: If matched systems repeatedly show visible failure before recoverability collapse under the stated perturbation protocol, this prediction fails for that system class.
records.next_external_test: Apply the same ordering test to an external time-series network dataset with known failure or degradation labels.
limitations: Current support is from deterministic toy systems.
External systems may require different visible failure markers.
non_claims: Does not claim HAOS-IIP proves biology.

records.title: Collapse-origin localization precedes global failure
records.prediction_statement: The earliest localized recoverability break should identify the sector, branch, or patch where later visible failure concentrates.
records.novelty_boundary: This predicts a diagnostic localization rule, not a new mechanism of failure.
records.perturbation: Localized or structured perturbation applied to a known branch, patch, or sector.
pass_criteria: the earliest local recoverability collapse occurs before global visible failure
the same local sector overlaps the later visible failure region
matched controls do not show the same localization by chance
fail_criteria: local recoverability collapse is spatially uncorrelated with later visible failure
global failure occurs without any prior local recoverability signal
the localization signal disappears under deterministic robustness variations
falsifiers: If local k_origin repeatedly fails to overlap later failure regions better than matched controls, this prediction fails for that system class.

current_evidence.result: fragile branch was designed to degrade earlier than whole-network failure

records.next_external_test: Add local-sector readouts to Lines B-D, then test on external degradation maps where failure regions are labeled.
limitations: Current evidence is design-level and internal.
Requires spatial or sector labels to test fairly.
non_claims: Does not claim causal proof from correlation.
Does not replace mechanistic failure analysis.

records.title: Safety margin decays before conventional threshold failure
records.prediction_statement: A safety_margin derived from recoverability collapse should approach zero before conventional visible failure thresholds are crossed.
records.novelty_boundary: This predicts a pre-failure margin observable. It does not claim that safety_margin is a conserved physical quantity.
system_scope: general weighted interaction graphs under monotone stress
records.perturbation: Controlled perturbation sweep with a defined collapse threshold and visible failure threshold.
pass_criteria: visible_failure occurs after safety_margin reaches zero
fail_criteria: visible_failure occurs while safety_margin is still positive
falsifiers: If visible failure consistently occurs before safety_margin reaches zero under the defined protocol, this prediction fails for that system class.

current_evidence.result: Lines A-D all record k_star before first visible failure.

records.next_external_test: Fit safety_margin on one perturbation family and test whether it forecasts visible failure on a held-out perturbation family.
limitations: Threshold choice affects k_star and safety_margin.
External calibration is required before operational use.
non_claims: Does not claim risk can be predicted without controls.
Does not claim a universal numerical threshold.
Does not replace existing safety analysis.

records.title: Recoverability gradients expose hidden fragile branches
records.prediction_statement: In coupled systems with a weak downstream branch, recoverability gradients should reveal branch degradation before whole-system function appears visibly impaired.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a diagnostic hypothesis about hidden fragility, not a claim that HAOS-IIP discovers biological or physical mechanisms by itself.
system_scope: interaction graphs with hub and branch motifs
records.perturbation: Progressive weakening of edges feeding a known fragile branch or weakly supported sector.
pass_criteria: branch_recoverability declines before whole-system visible failure
recoverability_gradient identifies the fragile branch before global collapse
matched non-fragile branches remain more stable under the same perturbation
fail_criteria: branch and whole-system recoverability decline at the same time
recoverability_gradient does not distinguish fragile from non-fragile branches
visible failure appears with no prior branch-level warning
falsifiers: If branch recoverability gives no earlier signal than whole-system readouts across matched fragile-branch systems, this prediction fails.

current_evidence.result: fragile downstream branch shows earlier degradation than the whole network in the Line A validation logic

records.next_external_test: Use a real or benchmark directed network with known vulnerable branches and compare branch recoverability against standard centrality or degree metrics.
limitations: Requires branch definitions or sector extraction.
Toy evidence is not field validation.
non_claims: Does not claim hidden branches exist in every system.
Does not claim causal mechanism without intervention.
Does not replace domain-specific fragility metrics.

records.title: Shell-native observables can close while raw local gradients remain open
records.prediction_statement: For some kernel-graph systems, shell-native recoverability observables should show stable closure under perturbation while raw local-gradient observables remain residual or open.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a physics-adjacent observable-frame prediction. It does not assert that the graph is physical spacetime or that closure proves a continuum law.
system_scope: discrete interaction graphs with shell or radial organization
external graph datasets where shell-like grouping can be independently defined
records.perturbation: Matched disorder, localized bump, or smooth inhomogeneity perturbations applied to graph observables.
pass_criteria: shell-native closure remains stable under defined perturbation
raw local-gradient readout remains open or residual under the same protocol
matched controls do not erase the split
fail_criteria: raw local-gradient and shell-native observables behave identically under controls
shell-native closure disappears under deterministic robustness checks
the split depends on post-hoc threshold tuning
falsifiers: If independently grouped shell-native observables fail to separate from raw local-gradient residuals under matched controls, this prediction fails for that graph class.

current_evidence.result: internal bridge separates shell-native closures from raw local-gradient open boundaries

records.next_external_test: Apply the same shell-native versus raw-gradient split to an independently generated graph family with pre-registered grouping rules.
limitations: Current evidence is internal to HAOS-IIP graph families.
Shell grouping must be pre-registered to avoid post-hoc closure.
non_claims: Does not claim a continuum limit.
Does not claim physical spacetime emergence.
Does not claim new physics without external replication.
